question: Instructor hypothesis (2026-08-18): simplifying the LLM's input should push the LLM and AGAF rungs below the feedback loop, making the ladder hold.
status: comparison_only - NOT the canonical UNSW result

text_levels.L0_rich: canonical kg_triples_nl.txt - prose + absolute magnitude cues + coarse levels (~380 chars/line)
text_levels.levels_only: prose + coarse levels, absolute magnitude cues removed (200 chars/line)
text_levels.bare_numbers: no prose, raw feature values only (93 chars/line)
text_levels.structure_only: endpoints + protocol/port only, traffic statistics removed (54 chars/line)

llm_access_axes.loop_full_llm_access: default: attention bias on flagged top-k edges (~8%) PLUS output fusion of the LLM branch on ALL edges
llm_access_axes.loop_8pct_llm_access: --no-output-fusion: attention bias on flagged top-k edges ONLY (~8% of edges)

findings: The target ordering (GNN < LLM < AGAF < loop) holds ONLY at L0 rich text. Every simplification level breaks it, and breaks it in the direction opposite to the hypothesis: AGAF ends up ABOVE the loop at all three simplified levels.

Simplifying the text does drag the LLM rung below the loop (L2: 0.4883 vs 0.6435; L3: 0.3947 vs 0.5369) - but only by dragging it below the GNN rung too (0.5496), which breaks the bottom of the ladder instead.
AGAF is far more robust to LLM simplification than the loop: from L0 to L3 the LLM falls 0.341, the loop falls 0.240, and AGAF falls only 0.182. AGAF never drops below the loop at any level.
L1 (levels_only) AGAF 0.7609 is HIGHER than L0 AGAF 0.7459, so the rich magnitude prose is not even optimal for fusion - removing it helped AGAF while hurting the LLM and the loop.

DECISIVE: with output fusion disabled, so the LLM reaches the loop only through the ~8% attention path, the loop collapses to 0.5343 at L0 - BELOW the GNN alone (0.5496). The same collapse holds at every text level (0.534-0.562).

That means the loop's advantage does not come from the iterative 8% semantic consultation at all; it comes from the all-edge output fusion of LLM embeddings. The premise that 'feedback only consults the LLM on 8% of the data' describes a mechanism that, in isolation, performs no better than the bare GNN.

At L3 the two axes converge (0.5369 full vs 0.5367 8%-only): once the LLM text is weak enough, output fusion contributes nothing, which is consistent with output fusion being the sole source of the loop's gain.

integrity.gnn_rung_constant_across_levels: 0.5496 (LLM-independent, used as the fixed reference line)
integrity.nl_text_label_free: asserted by knowledge_graph.assert_label_free for every variant
